entries.title: Some of Australia’s biggest companies are planning for an unbearable climate future
entries.content:
![](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756906/original/file-20260831-50-91skc4.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&rect=0%2C1%2C7643%2C5095&q=45&auto=format&w=1050&h=700&fit=crop)

[Andrew Merry/Getty](https://www.gettyimages.com.au/detail/photo/australia-red-outback-desert-aerial-royalty-free-image/2172770696?phrase=extreme%20heat%20australia&searchscope=image%2Cfilm&adppopup=true)

Even as unprecedented fires and heatwaves [rage across Europe](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-02/europe-fires-fingerprints-of-climate-change/106967040), scientists track [the retreat of Antarctic sea ice](https://www.smh.com.au/environment/climate-change/it-s-beginning-to-look-a-lot-like-the-future-fears-over-sudden-loss-of-sea-ice-20260815-p60ol1.html) and a [supercharged El Niño system](https://www.nine.com.au/australia-news/fears-huge-offshore-system-will-make-2026-the-warmest-year-on-record-20260818-p60pbg.html) heads our way, Australia’s largest companies are forecasting business-as-usual in a much hotter world.

Last year, Australia introduced mandatory [company climate reporting](https://standards.aasb.gov.au/aasb-s2-sep-2024). They must now disclose the climate “[risks and opportunities](https://theconversation.com/new-climate-reporting-rules-start-on-july-1-many-companies-are-not-ready-for-the-change-258706)” that may affect their prospects.

Several of Australia’s biggest energy and resource companies have now published new [sustainability reports](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kennethslee1_sustainabilityreporting-climatechange-activity-7492808780280188928-iaxy) as part of annual financial reporting.

Their disclosures reveal the climate future they are planning for, and whether this is aligned with international science-based targets such as the Paris Agreement’s [1.5°C warming threshold](https://unfccc.int/process-and-meetings/the-paris-agreement).

What we’re seeing is alarming.

## Companies planning for an unbearable future

Most of these reports indicate big companies are developing strategies on a climate change “base case” – a representation of what they consider most likely to happen – of more than 2°C of warming. The future temperature rise they’re planning for is one scientists say would deliver [an unbearably hot planet](https://globalclimaterisks.org/insights/blog/a-half-degree-increase-could-triple-uninhabitable-areas-on-earth/).

Some of Australia’s largest miners have followed this approach. Both [Rio Tinto](https://cdn-rio.dataweavers.io/-/media/content/documents/invest/reports/climate-change-reports/2025-annual-report-climate.pdf?rev=dd9be5ec39ee41a88f6abb356eceef8f) and [BHP](https://www.bhp.com/-/media/documents/investors/annual-reports/2026/260818_bhpannualreport2026.pdf) expect global temperature increases of more than 2°C by the end of the century.

Not every company reveals the increase in global temperature they are planning for. But even if they don’t, their disclosures show they’re not expecting temperatures to hold to 1.5°C.

Energy companies [AGL](https://www.agl.com.au/content/dam/digital/agl/documents/about-agl/investors/2026/260812-2026-annual-report.pdf) and [Origin Energy](https://www.originenergy.com.au/wp-content/uploads/95/Origin-Energy-FY26-Annual-Report.pdf) both express confidence their strategies and business models will remain robust, even if temperatures accelerate beyond 2.6°C warming. This increase would put the Australian economy, environment and community at [severe risk](https://theconversation.com/is-this-australias-climate-wake-up-call-official-report-reveals-a-hotter-harder-future-if-we-dont-act-now-256229).

[![Mining machinery suspended above a red pile of iron ore.](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756914/original/file-20260831-50-22jdlw.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&q=45&auto=format&w=754&fit=clip)](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756914/original/file-20260831-50-22jdlw.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&q=45&auto=format&w=1000&fit=clip)

The assumption that business-as-usual will be possible in a hotter world is out of step with the latest science.
[Cuhrig/Getty](https://www.gettyimages.com.au/detail/photo/reclaimer-on-iron-ore-mine-site-royalty-free-image/96277831?phrase=Australia%20and%20mining&searchscope=image%2Cfilm&adppopup=true)

## Companies hold power

Companies often argue that governments are [responsible for creating policy](https://climateintegrity.org.au/latest/media-release-risky-influence-report?) to address global warming. But this underestimates the power corporate leaders hold to shape Australia’s shared climate future through financial decisions.

For example, mining giant BHP [expects demand](https://www.bhp.com/-/media/documents/investors/annual-reports/2026/260818_bhpannualreport2026.pdf) for steelmaking coal to remain robust for decades, with customers from China, India and Southeast Asia. This underpins the valuation of its major export commodities, and appears to justify the lack of plans to scale down steelmaking coal production. However, this assumption sits uneasily with the fact these same countries have their [own net-zero targets](https://zerotracker.net/).

Similarly, Rio Tinto confirms “[no portfolio adjustments](https://cdn-rio.dataweavers.io/-/media/content/documents/invest/reports/climate-change-reports/2025-annual-report-climate.pdf?rev=dd9be5ec39ee41a88f6abb356eceef8f)” are made to its future production plans. Its central case estimate of 2.1–2.3°C of warming by 2100 assumes developing countries will miss or delay their stated net-zero targets, underwriting business-as-usual production for the company.

## Disclosures out of step with science

However, the assumption that business-as-usual will be possible in a hotter world is out of step with the latest science. The Paris Agreement’s temperature goal was set in 2015 based on [exhaustive scientific assessments](https://www.ipcc.ch/sr15/) that warming of more than 2°C would be dangerous, and limiting warming to 1.5°C was necessary to minimise climate risks.

Scientific knowledge about how much global warming is “safe” has [exponentially increased](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-environ-111523-102029). It reemphasises the need to keep to 1.5°C with “[limited overshoot](https://climateworkscentre.org/resource/what-does-overshooting-1-5c-mean/)”. This means we can only exceed 1.5°C temporarily, and simultaneously need to be working to bring temperatures back down. Only then will we minimise irreversible changes such as sea level rise, the disappearance of coral reefs or vast sea ice loss at the poles.

Scientific [best estimates](https://theconversation.com/overshooting-1-5-c-even-temporary-warming-above-globally-agreed-temperature-limit-could-have-permanent-consequences-255523) find we can’t go over 1.5°C by more than 0.1–0.3°C (a “peak temperature” of 1.6–1.8°C) and still return warming to safe levels. Even then, the longer we stay above 1.5°C and the extent to which we exceed this threshold, the more devastating the outcome.

## Is this legal?

Legally, there’s no issue with companies using a base case for planning that exceeds 2°C of warming. But this approach isn’t in line with Australia’s broader international legal obligations. Companies will likely face increased investor scrutiny or [reputational blowback](https://www.accr.org.au/research/investor-briefing-latest-insights-into-bhp%E2%80%99s-operational-decarbonisation-pathway/) when they walk back climate commitments.

In July 2025, the world’s highest court, the International Court of Justice (ICJ), confirmed [1.5°C is the temperature limit](https://www.icj-cij.org/case/187) countries are aiming for. To meet their Paris Agreement promises, governments — including Australia — have to show the most ambitious action the country can realistically take to help keep warming under 1.5°C. Australia’s [latest plan](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/climate-change/international-climate-action) for a 62–70% emissions cut from 2005 levels was submitted in September 2025.

The court confirmed the Paris Agreement also requires governments to take action at home to cut emissions in line with the 1.5°C goal — including [introducing rules for businesses](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/68100abb22fce2334c41ecdc/t/6a2a0c7eb2c43d470dd9fb37/1781140606273/Policy+backgrounder+June26+digital.pdf) operating in their countries. To follow international law, the Australian government needs to use every tool available to regulate the emissions of big companies, based on the best available science. Countries that don’t comply could be sued before the ICJ and ordered to pay compensation to other nations.

## What about Australia’s climate policy?

Big companies in Australia contribute [more than 30%](https://climateworkscentre.org/news/half-of-australias-biggest-companies-have-net-zero-emissions-plans-but-theres-more-to-be-done/) of our domestic emissions. If we also include emissions from the fossil fuels some of these companies produce, it raises Australia’s global carbon footprint to around 4.5% of global fossil [carbon dioxide emissions](https://climateanalytics.org/publications/australias-global-fossil-fuel-carbon-footprint), [second](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/article/2024/aug/12/australian-fossil-fuel-exports-ranked-second-globally-for-climate-damage-with-no-plan-for-reduction) only to Russia. Making sure big companies do their bit to reduce emissions is essential for Australia to meet its climate targets.

This year, Australia is the [“President of Negotiations” for COP31](https://unfccc-cop.dcceew.gov.au/cop31). This is an opportunity for Australia to show it’s doing all it can – internationally and in its own backyard – to support compliance with the Paris Agreement and accelerate climate action. From their new disclosures, it doesn’t seem that Australia’s biggest companies have got the memo.

![The Conversation](https://counter.theconversation.com/content/290234/count.gif)

She is affiliated with the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), serving as a Coordinating Lead Author in Working Group III (mitigation) for the IPCC's Seventh Assessment Report.*

entries.title: Two dead and at least 15 missing after flash flood in Arizona’s Grand Canyon
entries.content:
National Park Service confirms second death from weekend flash flood as area braces for more storms

A [second death was confirmed](https://x.com/GrandCanyonNPS/status/2094450492357185935) by National Park Service officials on Monday after [aflash flood](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/30/grand-canyon-flash-flood-arizona-people-missing-evacuated) sent a surge of water and debris through an area of the Grand Canyon over the weekend.

Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter during the deluge that consumed trails and infrastructure. Fifteen people are still missing or unaccounted for, as more heavy rain and thunderstorms in the [forecasts threaten additional debris flows, flash floods or rockfalls](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/significant-flash-flooding-closes-phantom-ranch-and-north-kaibab-trail.htm), the NPS said in a statement.

[Continue reading...](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/31/grand-canyon-storms-flash-flood)

entries.title: Microsoft Outlook Is Down
entries.content:
If you're trying to check your inbox or send an email in Microsoft Outlook, only to find the app uncooperative, you're not alone. Outlook is currently down for many users as of Monday afternoon. That's apparent to anyone who can't get the app to work: Downdetector, which highlights user reports for app outages, [shows tens of thousands of reports](https://downdetector.com/status/outlook/ "open in a new window") as of 3:00 p.m. ET, and while the rate of reports does seem to be decreasing, thousands of reports keep coming in with every refresh.

[As CNET reports](https://www.cnet.com/news-live/microsoft-outlook-exchange-online-service-outage/ "open in a new window"), Microsoft has officially confirmed the outage itself. The company [posted on its Microsoft 365 Status X account](https://x.com/MSFT365Status/status/2094455556454920701 "open in a new window"), stating: “We’ve identified an issue with an authentication component which is contributing to impact. To address this, we’ve developed a remediation strategy, and we’re applying it to a portion of infrastructure to test its efficacy. Once we’ve confirmed this resolves impact, we’ll apply the solution more broadly. For more information, please see EX1464935 in the admin center.”

As such, the company should be rolling out a fix in due time, though it's difficult to say how long that may be. Recent outages have been fixed in a matter of hours, while others have stretched into the following day. At the time of writing, Downdetector shows that 38% of users are reporting issues receiving messages in Outlook, while 24% report issues with the app, and 21% with logging in.

As it happens, Outlook isn't the only Microsoft product facing issues: Users report that Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Store, Microsoft Azur and Microsoft 365 in general are experiencing issues. In addition, OpenAI users are reporting issues with ChatGPT.

entries.title: Apple ninja edits Mac Studio specs to remove PCIe Gen 6 storage reference
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

During Apple [surprise Mac announcements](https://www.macworld.com/article/3220024/apple-announces-the-m5-ultra-mac-studio-with-up-to-512gb-of-ram.html) last week, the company declared in its press release that the Mac Studio features “a next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6.” However, that mention has since been removed from the Mac Studio press release and site, as spotted by [MacGeneration](https://www.macg.co/mac/2026/08/non-le-mac-studio-nest-pas-pcie-60-cetait-surement-une-erreur-dans-le-communique-310617).

The PCIe Gen 6 statement has been removed from the Apple U.K., Apple Germany, and Apple Japan press releases, though strangely, the PCIe Gen 6 reference still exists in the Apple France [press release](https://www.apple.com/fr/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-new-mac-studio-with-m5-max-and-m5-ultra/). The releases still list August 25, 2026, as the day of publication and have no record of an update, but we, along with many other outlets, quoted the PCIe Gen 6 in our original stories and haven’t been contacted by Apple about a correction.

The press release now reads, “Storage performance is up to twice as fast, with a next-generation SSD architecture, delivering industry-leading read and write speeds for rapid project loading, file transfers, and loading huge LLMs.” The twice as fast comparision is to the M3 Ultra Mac Studio.

The Internet Archive has a [copy](https://web.archive.org/web/20260825130329/https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-new-mac-studio-with-m5-max-and-m5-ultra/) of the U.S. Mac Studio press release, recorded on August 25 at 13:03:29, and it contains the PCIe Gen 6 reference. Other copies recorded by the Internet Archive on August 25 still have the reference, but the first [record](https://web.archive.org/web/20260826020313/https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-new-mac-studio-with-m5-max-and-m5-ultra/) of the press release on August 26 at 02:03:13 shows that the release was revised to remove references to PCIe Gen 6.

PCIe Gen 6 is the next generation of the PCIe interconnect standard, offering performance upgrades over the PCIe Gen 5 standard. Apple did not specify that the M5 Ultra Mac Studio implements PCIe Gen 5, but the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips are equipped with it. So it’s likely that the M5 Ultra has it too, and Apple made an error in its press release.

Apple was contacted for clarification and had yet to respond at the time of this posting.

entries.title: Kalshi Dishes Out Its First-Ever Lifetime Ban to George Santos
entries.content:
Kalshi has issued its first-ever lifetime ban to former U.S. Rep. George Santos after concluding he failed to fully cooperate with an insider-trading investigation. He is also being fined $71,356, according to a filing (PDF) on its website. Engadget reports:
It was reported in June that Santos was under investigation from the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) over insider trading. Prediction markets like Kalshi allow users to buy contracts or shares in the outcome of events. Participants don't necessarily have to wait for an event to resolve before selling these contracts and cashing in.
Santos allegedly bought contracts on Kalshi indicating that he would not attend this year's State of the Union speech after weather disrupted his travel plans. According to the CFTC, Santos then sold those contracts for a profit after claiming on social media that he would be in attendance. The former congressman is said to have made more than $17,500 through this scheme, which Kalshi reportedly detected and flagged to authorities. In July, Santos agreed to pay over $35,000 to settle the CFTC's claims against him. The agency also issued him a three-year trading ban.
Kalshi, however, doesn't plan to allow Santos back on its platform in 2029 (or anytime after that). The company confirmed to The Wall Street Journal this was the first time it had given anyone a lifetime ban and that it did so because Santos didn't fully cooperate with its investigation. He can appeal the decision to the CTFC.

entries.title: MCP was supposed to solve the agent tooling problem. It missed a step.
entries.content:
![Abstract nodes](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/08/153448f0-guerrillabuzz-rivsjtigwlc-unsplash-1024x576.jpg)

Connecting an AI agent to a tool is relatively straightforward. Things get more complicated once an organization has hundreds or thousands of resources spread across different clouds and platforms. Agentic Resource Discovery, or ARD, is meant to help agents find their way through all of that.

AWS highlighted the open specification in its August 31 [Weekly Roundup](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-weekly-roundup-welcome-ducklabs-to-the-team-agentic-resource-discovery-ard-and-more-august-31-2026/) after taking a deeper technical look at it a week earlier, describing the idea as “DNS, but for agents.” Instead of telling an agent where to find everything ahead of time, ARD lets it search across different registries for what it needs.

And despite AWS highlighting the project, ARD isn’t an AWS technology. It was authored by [Junjie Bu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/junjiebu/) of Google, [R.V. Guha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/r-v-guha-59b19412/) of Microsoft and [Shaun Smith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/smithshaun/) of Hugging Face, and released under the Apache 2.0 license. Engineers from several other companies have helped shape the project, including Cisco, Databricks, GitHub, GoDaddy, [Nvidia](https://thenewstack.io/nvidia-hugging-face-acquisition-neutrality/), Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.

AWS’s role, at least so far, has been to provide feedback on the specification and explore how it could work with its own Agent Registry. The goal is to make the registries that already exist work together.

> Instead of telling an agent where to find everything ahead of time, ARD lets it search across different registries for what it needs.

## MCP skips the discovery step

The [Model Context Protocol](https://thenewstack.io/mistral-mcp-connector-migration/) has become a common way for AI applications to connect to external tools and data, but it assumes the client already knows which server it wants to use. That becomes a problem as companies [spread their infrastructure across clouds](https://thenewstack.io/enterprise-ai-agent-governance/), SaaS platforms and internal systems.

ARD helps an agent find a resource before it tries to use it. The specification uses the term “agentic resource” for anything an AI client can connect to, from an MCP server to other outside capabilities. An ARD-compatible service keeps track of what’s available instead of requiring developers to set up every connection in advance.

> The Model Context Protocol has become a common way for AI applications to connect to external tools and data, but it assumes the client already knows which server it wants to use.

## Federation without forced migration

Companies can keep their own catalogs and policies while routing searches to other ARD-compatible services. An enterprise, for example, could keep internal resources private while searching approved external catalogs when needed. AWS calls this “describe once, discover everywhere.”

The current v0.91 proposal, dated August 26, uses JSON-LD and a REST interface. Its required POST /search endpoint searches by task, while optional endpoints allow clients to browse available resources.

Each discovery service can set its own rules for what it returns and which sources it trusts. This is also where AWS’s DNS comparison falls short. A domain name points to a specific location, while an ARD search could turn up several options that all appear capable of doing the job.

## Route 53 engineers shaped ARD

The DNS comparison has some history behind it. Two of the three authors of AWS’s August 24 ARD post work closely with Route 53. Principal software engineer [Jeffrey Damick](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeffreydamick/) focuses on DNS and networking technologies, while [Bhargav Talluri](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bhargavt/) leads product management for Route 53, as well as for agent identity and discovery in AWS Agent Registry.

Agent Registry already gives AWS customers a central view of their resources. Adding ARD could bring resources running elsewhere into that view without requiring companies to register everything with AWS.

> Adding ARD could bring resources running elsewhere into that view without requiring companies to register everything with AWS.

ARD’s governance is still being worked out, with board terms and membership among the details yet to be settled. The group has also discussed eventually moving the project to a neutral organization such as the W3C or an AI foundation.

## Finding tools before using them

AWS is already exploring how it could connect with Agent Registry and [find resources outside its own catalog](https://thenewstack.io/cloudflare-ai-web-economics/).

There may not be much time to settle on a common approach, since connecting all these directories will only get harder once companies have built their own discovery systems.

The post [MCP was supposed to solve the agent tooling problem. It missed a step.](https://thenewstack.io/ard-agent-discovery-specification/) appeared first on [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io).

entries.title: Google’s new forecasting model beats everyone. You can’t use it at work (yet).
entries.content:
![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/08/d2018a71-insaanu-studio-mavfx_zrdea-unsplash-1024x626.jpg)

On Monday, Google launched [TimesFM-3](https://research.google/blog/timesfm-3-a-zero-shot-foundation-model-for-multivariate-forecasting/), a 330-million-parameter time-series forecasting model trained on over a trillion real-world and synthetic data time points.

The new model is now available on Hugging Face under a non-commercial license.

Large language models are great at predicting the next word. For businesses, time-series forecasting models essentially try to do the same thing, but for data. Over the last few years, there’s been a lot of work in building better forecasting models. Last year saw the launch of models like Chronos-2 from Amazon and Moirai 2.0 from Salesforce, while, more recently, Datadog launched its [Toto 2.0 model](https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/ai/toto-2/).

These models represent a relatively new breed of forecasting models in that they can ingest multiple time series. As Google research scientists Ayush Jain and Rajat Sen explain in the announcement, “most real-world forecasting problems are inherently multivariate: where multiple time series and auxiliary external features jointly impact the future forecast of a time series.”

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/08/5c4f141b-timesfm3_promotionsgraph.width-1250.png)

Past sales, they explain, only tell part of the story. “A good forecast should also draw on sales of related products (e.g., ice cream cones, syrups), historical foot traffic, and known future events like weather forecasts, promotions, and holidays.”

TimesFM-3 is Google’s first model that was natively pre-trained to handle these multiple time series and do so with zero-shot generalizations. This also allows it to forecast multiple related time series in parallel and include historical data like past foot traffic.

In the benchmarks Google shared, TimesFM-3 outperforms all of these, often by a significant margin. The team looked at Salesforce’s Gift-Eval, Amazon/AutoGluon’s FEV-Bench, and Time.

What’s maybe the most surprising here is that TimesFM-2.5, which was state-of-the-art when it launched in September 2025, is now at the bottom of the benchmarks. That’s how fast this field is developing.

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/08/bf5024b2-timesfm35_time.width-1250-1024x680.png)

## The architecture

Like its predecessors, TimesFM-3 is a decoder-only transformer that chops each time series into patches of 32 data points and treats them roughly the way a language model treats tokens.

What’s new is that these tokens now flow through two alternating kinds of attention layers. The first one looks backward across time within a single series and keeps things strictly causal, so the model can’t see values it shouldn’t know yet. The other looks sideways across all series at a given moment, which is how a promotion in one product line, for example, can inform the forecast for another.

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/08/d1af83a9-timesfm31_architecture.width-1250-1024x573.png)

Decoding changed, too. Earlier versions generated forecasts one patch at a time, Google’s researchers explain, which added latency and compounded errors along the way.

Instead, TimesFM-3 appends masked placeholder tokens for the entire forecast horizon and then fills them all in with a single forward pass.

## The non-commercial license

Google decided to launch the new model [under a non-commercial license](https://huggingface.co/google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch/blob/main/LICENSE). That’s becoming a bit of a [trend](https://thenewstack.io/glm-5-3-flash-chinese-chips/) in the world of model builders.

TimesFM-2.5 still shipped with the [Apache 2.0 license](https://github.com/google-research/timesfm) — as do Toto 2.0 and Chronos-2.

The TimesFM-3 source code is still under the Apache license, but Google notes that “for the time being, TimesFM 3.0 pretrained weights are distributed under the separate `timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0` license and are restricted to non-commercial, non-production use. Commercial or production use of the default pretrained weights is **not permitted**.”

Google will soon replace TimesFM-2.5 as the model that powers BitQuery’s [AI.FORECAST](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-ai-forecast) command, so the company is actively monetizing these models.

That’s not unusual, of course. Every player in this market already integrates its forecasting models into its own platform, but Google restricting the state-of-the-art weights while also opening a paid path through its data warehouse is a pretty clear signal of where these labs think the money is in the long run.

The post [Google’s new forecasting model beats everyone. You can’t use it at work (yet).](https://thenewstack.io/google-timesfm-3-multivariate-forecasting/) appeared first on [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io).

entries.content:
"You fail if you build for where the models are now. You fail if you build for where you think the models will be in a year. The only way to build is for where the models will be in 2-3 months."  
  
— [@OpenAI](https://x.com/OpenAI)'s ChatGPT Work product lead [@tarstarr](https://x.com/tarstarr)

[Your browser does not support the video tag.](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2094467962216542208/vid/avc1/1920x1080/Xs8bxn5nmWA5t0rE.mp4?tag=29)

![Lenny Rachitsky](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1592990461517389824/iln8hi1f_normal.jpg)

Lenny Rachitsky@lennysan

"Are you mainlining it yet?"  
  
This is one of the key internal memes at [@OpenAI](https://x.com/OpenAI), and a big part of the reason there's been a vibe shift toward Codex over the past few months.  
  
It asks: are you using the product all day, every day? Are you depending on it? Are you bringing all your taste to bear on whether this is something people actually want?  
  
Tara Seshan ([@tarstarr](https://x.com/tarstarr)) leads product for Codex and ChatGPT work at OpenAI (alongside her EM [@ajambrosino](https://x.com/ajambrosino)). When I asked her what changed internally to shift the vibes toward Codex, her answer was: nothing. People just started noticing.  
  
In our conversation, we also discuss:  
🔸 Her rule for building on top of frontier models: build for where they'll be in 2-3 months—building for today fails, building for a year out fails  
🔸 Why PMs are now in the business of elevating everyone's ambition  
🔸 Why the future of knowledge work is steering, not rowing  
🔸 Why OpenAI is "founders-led," not founder-led (and why there's no secret strategy room)  
🔸 The one type of writing she will never let AI touch

Interesting paper from Tencent.

Tencent trains an agent to manage its own working context, and assi...
entries.content:
Interesting paper from Tencent.  
  
Tencent trains an agent to manage its own working context, and assigns credit at the level of individual context edits.  
  
Long-horizon tasks force a model to retrieve, integrate and maintain scattered information across many turns, and keeping every interaction history makes the working context grow without bound.  
  
Recent proactive methods let a model edit its own context with tools, but the toolset stops at search, deletion and summarization.  
  
ContextPilot adds global planning, long-term memory and adaptive soft compression, so the agent can offload information rather than only discard it.  
  
The training side is where it gets interesting. Standard RL hands the final trajectory reward to every intermediate edit equally. ContextPilot uses context and entropy variation to find which editing decisions actually mattered, samples branches at those points, and estimates action-level advantages from all branched trajectories passing through that edit.  
  
On long-context QA and deep search it beats existing baselines across several base models while holding a more compact working context. Code is available.  
  
Paper: [arxiv.org/abs/2608.28476](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28476)

entries.title: National Parks commemorate ties to WWII ahead of 85th Pearl Harbor anniversary
entries.content:
The United States’ 63 official [National Parks](https://www.popsci.com/environment/july-yellowstone-park-deadliest-month/) are often renowned for their [natural beauty](https://www.popsci.com/environment/lupine-superbloom-redwood-national-park/), but many of them are also hubs of history. To help honor both the [country’s 250th birthday](https://www.popsci.com/technology/limited-edition-july-fourth-quarters/) and the upcoming 85th anniversary of the attack on [Pearl Harbor](https://www.popsci.com/environment/pearl-harbor-wwii-logbooks-weather-dat/), more than a dozen locations are participating in World War II Across America’s National Parks. According to a [recent announcement](https://www.facebook.com/PearlHarborNPS/posts/pfbid031CXfgLn68xGhzWqN9EMfr4kfkpvAi2SkpNW32HKbeufioJ1hsz889ajLefDjJDDql?rdid=GXB8r8Ngh8TMuA9e), three parks from around the country will highlight “different parts of America’s wartime story, including both triumphs and tragedies” every week leading up to December 7.

“This list of parks is by no means exclusive, nor are the stories that will be shared,” park representatives wrote on social media. “They represent just a fraction of the war’s impact on our parks and the nation, with many of those impacts still felt today.”

While the project began with the [Pearl Harbor National Memorial](https://www.facebook.com/PearlHarborNPS/posts/pfbid0HWqVBfiTUwoFaXtyVfqj5EmQo1mv6woCeMbNey3GxSVrrV9WBLXDBQ4vEyqi4LUPl?rdid=CVP2SFUYvDGIxqYQ) itself, the two subsequent entries are arguably lesser known for their relationships to WWII—[Governors Island National Monument](https://www.facebook.com/governorsislandnps/posts/pfbid0Vf8etg12Y8svMujbRJyxHajUTS9L2LutcH5qQBoLaTi5DCY9Pa4hfxKyHJTLSR7Rl?rdid=FCkjfMmD4p7PmLFP) in New York and [Golden Gate Recreation Area](https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1CNghEYTgF/) in California.

## An eastern military headquarters

Located in New York Harbor near Lower Manhattan, [Governors Island National Monument](https://www.facebook.com/governorsislandnps/posts/pfbid0Vf8etg12Y8svMujbRJyxHajUTS9L2LutcH5qQBoLaTi5DCY9Pa4hfxKyHJTLSR7Rl?rdid=FCkjfMmD4p7PmLFP) commemorates the location of the Eastern Theater of Operations, later renamed the Eastern Defense Command in 1942. The U.S. established the military headquarters here two weeks after the attack on Pearl Harbor. This headquarters oversaw protecting the then 40 states, Washington D.C., as well as Army bases in Bermuda, Iceland, Greenland, and Newfoundland.

Governors Island also oversaw New York City’s defensive brownouts and blackouts to guard residents against any suspected aerial bombardments.

![New York, UNITED STATES: Governors Island is pictured 11 May 2006 in New York harbor with lower Manhattan (L) in background. According to the National Park Service, Governors Island was the command headquarters and military post for the United States Army from 1794 until 1966. From 1966 to 1996 it was the US Coast Guard?s largest and most complex installation. In 2003, the island was sold and transferred to two parties: 22 acres, designated as the Governors Island National Monument, to the US Secretary of the Interior, and managed by the National Park Service; and 150 acres to the Governors Island Preservation and Education Corporation, a corporation formed jointly by the State and City of New York. Today, city, state and federal agencies are in the planning stages of converting this former military installation into new public parkland. AFP PHOTO/Stan HONDA (Photo credit should read STAN HONDA/AFP via Getty Images)](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Governors-Island-Park.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*According to the National Park Service, Governors Island was the command headquarters and military post for the United States Army from 1794 until 1966. From 1966 to 1996 it was the US Coast Guard’s largest and most complex installation. Credit: [STAN HONDA/AFP via Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/new-york-united-states-governors-island-is-pictured-11-may-news-photo/57597365?adppopup=true)* STAN HONDA

## Anti-submarine nets, blackouts, and other domestic defences

On the other side of the country,the [Golden Gate Recreation Area](https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1CNghEYTgF/), was vital to the West Coast’s domestic defense during WWII. At the newly established Fort Cronkhite, thousands of troops in the Harbor Defenses of San Francisco mandated evening blackouts around the Bay Area, while maintaining an anti-submarine net, anti-aircraft weapons, and 600 underwater mines. The fort also included two 500-pound battery guns that were ready to aim at any potential incoming enemy naval vessels. Even today, many of the site’s hastily built, temporary wooden structures are still used by non-profit and educational park partners.

![Sign for Golden Gate National Recreation Area near Crissy Field, in the Presidio, San Francisco, California, June 28, 2020. (Photo by Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Golden-Gate-Recreation-Sign.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

*A sign for Golden Gate National Recreation Area near Crissy Field, in the Presidio, San Francisco, California. Credit: [Smith Collection/Gado via Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/sign-for-golden-gate-national-recreation-area-near-crissy-news-photo/1253533570?adppopup=true)* Smith Collection/Gado

To keep up with the series, the National Park Service recommends following the #WWIINPS and #Freedom250 hashtags on social media. Next up for celebration: the [Redwood National and State Parks](https://www.popsci.com/environment/lupine-superbloom-redwood-national-park/).

The post [National Parks commemorate ties to WWII ahead of 85th Pearl Harbor anniversary](https://www.popsci.com/science/national-parks-world-war-ii-governors-island-golden-gate/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: History-making mother bear could be big Fat Bear Week 2026 contender
entries.content:
We are mere [weeks away from Fat Bear Week 2026](https://www.popsci.com/environment/new-fat-bear-week-childrens-book-brooke-hartman/), but the brown bears (*Ursus arctos*) [gorging on salmon at Katmai National Park and Preserve](https://www.popsci.com/environment/fat-bear-week-live-cam/) in Alaska are already showing off that beautiful bulk. Based on a [recent video](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcqmMmroOis/?igsi=MWxydHQzN2FiMGFhMQ==) posted by explore.org, [Bear #910](https://katmaiconservancy.org/bear-910) might be a major contender for this year’s competition.

Bear #910 is a female brown bear that was first spotted in 2019 at Katmai’s Brooks River. She is [about 10.5-years-old](https://katmai-bearcams.fandom.com/wiki/910#2026:_10.5_Year-Old_Single_Adult_Female), has large, blonde, floppy ears, which can help viewers pick her out of the crowd on the live cam set up in the park.

Bear #910 is [also a particularly unique mother bear.](https://mashable.com/article/fat-bear-week-katmai-bear-story) Between mid-August and October 2022, she [adopted her sister Bear #909’s 2.5-year-old female yearling cub](https://katmaiconservancy.org/bear-910) (a one- to two-year-old cub still with its mother), while she herself had a spring cub (a first-year cub that was born over the winter and emerges in the spring). An adoption like this is an exceptionally rare event in the wild, but it has also been [observed in polar bears](https://www.popsci.com/environment/rare-polar-bear-adoption-canada/). The pair was frequently seen fishing together with their cubs throughout 2023 and 2024 and a paper on their story was published in the journal [*BioOne*](https://bioone.org/journals/ursus/volume-2025/issue-36e5/URSUS-D-24-00007R1/Bonding-behavior-of-sister-brown-bears-with-different-aged-offspring/10.2192/URSUS-D-24-00007R1.full) in 2025.

Most bear mothers generally keep their litters separated, and this year’s season was an example of why they tend to stick to themselves. On Tuesday, July 28, the live-cams captured a [young brown bear cub being killed and eaten by an unrelated mother bear](https://www.popsci.com/environment/bear-cub-killed-katmai-brooks-river-bear-806/) (Bear #806). The deceased cub was born this spring, and was one of Bear #909’s cubs. Bear 909 started this season with two cubs, but has now lost both.

On Sunday, August 2, [one of Bear #335’s (also known as Jolly) cubs died](https://www.popsci.com/environment/katmai-mother-bear-attacks-335-cub/), after following three unrelated cubs up a tree. The mother of the cubs already in the tree attacked Bear #335’s cub, who did not survive the encounter. The identity of the mother bear who killed the spring cub was not confirmed.

Following the first cub’s death, naturalist Mike Fitz and park rangers Christine Loberg and Sarah Bruce hosted a chat about the incident. The team said that while infanticide by female adults does occur, this is likely the first documented case occurring at Brooks River. While there is no single answer as to [why mother bears are killing cubs](https://www.popsci.com/environment/why-mama-bears-kill-cubs/), some experts suspect bear adoption, food scarcity, and fights for dominance all play a role.

During [Fat Bear Week 2025](https://explore.org/fat-bear-week-schedule), she lost to Bear #856 in the second round of voting. Voting this year. The competition this year is scheduled to begin at the end of September.

The post [History-making mother bear could be big Fat Bear Week 2026 contender](https://www.popsci.com/environment/bear-910-fat-bear-week-contender-2026/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: New evidence shows OpenAI's trade secret theft & destruction of evidence, says Apple
entries.content:
Apple has been urging the court to require expedited discovery, and information discovered on Chang Liu's work MacBook suggests OpenAI is actively destroying evidence.  
  

![Glowing multicolored abstract orb with intertwined light trails at center of a dark background, resembling a futuristic digital assistant or voice interface icon](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68786-144931-SiriGPT-xl.jpg)  
Apple has sued OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft

  
OpenAI poached over 400 employees from Apple to work on AI projects, and two were called out in a trade secret theft [lawsuit in July](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/07/10/apple-sues-openai-previous-vp-of-product-design-over-mass-ip-theft). Apple has suggested the case needs urgent attention, and that [every delay](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/08/26/openais-lawsuit-delays-cause-more-harm-every-day-says-apple) causes more harm.  
  
According to a [new filing](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.cand.474095/gov.uscourts.cand.474095.94.1.pdf) from Apple on Monday, the MacBook used by Chang Liu has a lot of evidence that has allegedly been ignored by defendants so far. OpenAI has been [pushing back](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/08/06/openai-fires-back-says-apple-is-suing-because-it-cant-compete) on Apple's attempts for expedited discovery, which Apple now asserts could be due to an active attempt to destroy evidence.

entries.title: Review: Coyote vs. Acme is an unabashed love letter to Looney Tunes
entries.content:
It took three years, but [*Coyote vs. Acme*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coyote_vs._Acme) is finally in theaters and delighting audiences of all ages with its irresistible blend of slapstick humor, pointed satire, and even a warm fuzzy here and there. We're happy to report that the film was worth the wait.

**(Some spoilers below but no major reveals.)**

The film is based on a [well-known satirical piece](https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1990/02/26/coyote-v-acme) by Ian Frazier (also titled “Coyote vs. Acme”) published in The New Yorker in 1990. Development of a film version didn’t start until 2018, but some pretty talented people worked on the script, including James Gunn. Small wonder that Warner Bros.’ bizarre 2023 decision to shelve the film in order to take a tax write-off sparked outrage both within the industry and among fans online.

entries.title: Trump tells FCC to punish journalist for calling his election results "mixed"
entries.content:
President Trump yesterday demanded that the Federal Communications Commission punish or rebuke an NBC journalist for saying he has "mixed results" in his election endorsements. In the latest example of how Trump is using the FCC to harass reporters and news organizations that he dislikes, he said *Meet the Press* host Kristen Welker "will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment" for what he claimed was a "purposeful inaccuracy."

"Kristen Welker, the Unpopular 'Hostess' of the once great Meet the Press, now considered Meet the Fake Press, just stated that Donald Trump has 'mixed results' on his Endorsements of Candidates, when the recent WINS of Darline Graham and Mike Mazzei, stand at 100% for the U.S. Senate, and 98% for the U.S. House, recently and over the longterm. How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given Public Airwaves? Results are attached. Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment," Trump wrote in a [Truth Social post](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117184581053116309).

A separate [post](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117184527741564500) from Trump yesterday said, "THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA ARE OUT OF CONTROL, AND SOMETHING MUST BE DONE ABOUT IT. FCC TO THE RESCUE! President DJT." Trump also [posted a rant](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117175050400064794) on Friday about New York Times journalist Maggie Haberman, calling her "an unattractive person both inside and out" who "should be forced to turn over any and all money that she’s made through her fake reporting on me." Trump referred to Haberman throughout his post as "Maggot Haberman."

## Is Labor Day a good time to buy appliances?

Yes. Labor Day is traditionally one of the strongest sale periods for major appliances, with retailers often discounting outgoing models to make room for fall inventory. Compare prices across retailers and factor in delivery, installation, and haul-away fees before buying.

## Do Labor Day deals get better closer to the holiday?

Sometimes, but not always. Retailers may add short-term discounts or price-match competitors over the holiday weekend, but popular sizes and colors can sell out. If a price is a record low—or close to one—it is usually safer to buy rather than wait.

## When does Amazon’s Labor Day sale start?

Early [Labor Day sales](https://lifehacker.com/labor-day) have already started, with additional offers often appearing in the days closer to Labor Day. More retailers are likely to start their own sales leading up to the holiday on Monday, Sept. 7. Amazon does not follow one fixed public start date for a single Labor Day sale.

entries.title: What is pheromone-maxxing? The no-shower trend, explained.
entries.content:
![Chin, hand and sweating with sports person outdoor in nature closeup for exercise or fitness. Cardio, challenge and intense with athlete wiping perspiration from skin for marathon training or workout](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06bUUrMUJA0y2N3FfXerrJ8/hero-image.jpg)

Getting ready for a date usually comes with a fairly predictable checklist: Take a shower, apply deodorant, and find a shirt that has recently been through the washing machine. But one corner of the internet would like men to reconsider all three.

Meet ["pheromone-maxxing,"](https://www.tiktok.com/@raphislittle/video/7660267667864997133?_r=1&_t=ZP-99LK7YU9Cr1) the latest ["maxxing"](https://mashable.com/article/friction-maxxing-how-to) trend circulating among some young men online. The idea is to [skip showers](https://www.tiktok.com/@sasukeblunts/video/7671712461048794382?_r=1&_t=ZP-99LYWgagNTC), avoid deodorant, or wear dirty clothes in hopes of [amplifying their natural pheromones](https://www.tiktok.com/@dr_comp/video/7671102539575610637?_r=1&_t=ZP-99LYRSuGfoV) and making themselves [more attractive to potential partners.](https://www.tiktok.com/@true.angularity/video/7650793712729083166?_r=1&_t=ZP-99LYUcq3JOR)

Pheromones are chemical signals released by an organism that can affect the behavior or physiology of another member of the same species. They are well documented in many animals, but scientists have not conclusively identified a human sex pheromone. Still, pheromone-maxxers believe their natural scent will increase the pheromones they emit and, in turn, make them more attractive.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/Mary_is_Queen/status/2093843619798974926 "(Opens in a new tab)")

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/SpeechWrx/status/2094455711732297918 "(Opens in a new tab)")

It is certainly one way to make a first impression. But the pitch takes a real phenomenon — the role scent can play in attraction — and stretches it much further than the science currently supports.

Pheromone-maxxing has emerged alongside the broader rise of [looksmaxxing](https://mashable.com/video/stephen-colbert-looksmaxxing-manosphere), an online culture in which boys and young men try to optimize their appearance through skincare, exercise, cosmetic procedures, and sometimes risky DIY practices, all in pursuit of becoming more attractive.

SEE ALSO:
[The Looksmaxxing Glossary: Every term you need to understand the internet's most unhinged subculture](https://mashable.com/article/looksmaxxing-glossary-clavicular)

The most basic version of pheromone-maxxing involves giving up products that mask a person's natural scent, including cologne and deodorant. Some stop washing their hair, while others avoid showering for days at a time.

"Stopped washing my hair at all and now I unironically get more compliments on how it smells and looks (from women)," [one TikTok user wrote](https://www.tiktok.com/embed/v2/7581085899895721238). "Pheromone maxxing is key."

Another creator [claimed](https://www.tiktok.com/@r3mmybo1/video/7662234884005547294) that men cannot "pull baddies" because they wear cologne and deodorant. One adolescent described going three days without showering, then bathing and putting the same shirt back on to create what he called a ["halo effect of pheromones."](https://www.parents.com/why-some-teen-boys-are-skipping-showers-in-the-name-of-pheromone-maxxing-11810362)

Not everyone stops there. More extreme accounts promote wearing [unwashed clothing for long stretches](https://www.tiktok.com/@fluffdumpster/video/7352962089637465387) or even [drinking urine](https://www.vice.com/en/article/introducing-pheromone-maxxing-tiktoks-latest-disgusting-dating-trend/) in an attempt to "sweat out toxins." Those appear to be fringe extensions of the idea rather than a standard pheromone-maxxing routine, and neither is supported by scientific evidence.

It is also difficult to tell how many people are seriously following any version of the practice. Some creators appear sincere, while others may be joking, rage-baiting, or borrowing looksmaxxing language to attract attention. Social media commenters insist that almost nobody is actually doing it. Still, enough people appear to be taking the idea seriously that it is worth examining whether the supposed strategy can actually work.

## Can "pheromone-maxxing" work?

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/ThorTorrens/status/2094136423314079932 "(Opens in a new tab)")

Pheromones are chemical signals released by an organism that can trigger a behavioral or physiological response in another member of the same species. They are well documented in many animals, including insects, where they can communicate everything from danger and food locations to readiness to mate.

Whether humans produce and respond to pheromones in the same way is much less clear. Evolutionary biologist Tristram Wyatt wrote in a [2015 scientific review](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rspb.2014.2994) that humans may well have pheromones because we are mammals, but scientists have yet to conclusively identify a human sex pheromone or demonstrate that one reliably produces a romantic response.

That does not mean our individual body odors have no effect on how other people perceive us: In the [1995 "sweaty T-shirt study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7630893/)", women smelled shirts worn by men and generally preferred the scents of those whose major histocompatibility complex, or MHC, genes differed from their own. These genes play an important role in the immune system and may also influence a person’s body odor.

Yet, subsequent research is mixed. For example, a [2020 meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32306884/) found no overall evidence that people choose partners with different MHC genes, nor a consistent preference for the body odor of genetically dissimilar people.

Unfortunately for those jumping on this trend, what builds up when you stop showering isn't a proven supply of pheromones. Sweat itself is odorless — body odor only develops when sweat mixes with bacteria living on your skin, according to the [Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/17865-body-odor). As dermatologist Dr. Shereen Teymour [told USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/health-wellness/2026/08/31/gen-z-men-pheromone-maxxing-skipping-showers-women/91464620007/), "For the most part, [this trend is] bacteria-maxxing." Skip basic hygiene for too long and you're also risking inflamed hair follicles, irritation in skin folds, and skin infections. Definitely *not* attractive.

## How did we get here?

The larger "looksmaxxing" trend comes from an online self-improvement subculture that first developed in incel ("involuntarily celibate,") forums. Those communities frequently promoted the "black pill," a fatalistic belief that appearance and genetics largely determine a man’s romantic and social future.

Within that worldview, looksmaxxing offered users a way to improve their odds. Members rank facial features, calculate their supposed "sexual market value," and share strategies for "ascending," or becoming attractive enough to move higher in the community’s rigid hierarchy.

SEE ALSO:
[The Looksmaxxing Glossary: Every term you need to understand the internet's most unhinged subculture](https://mashable.com/article/looksmaxxing-glossary-clavicular)

That can include advice most people would recognize as ordinary grooming. "Softmaxxing" covers practices such as exercising, improving a skincare routine, getting a flattering haircut, dressing well, and taking care of one’s teeth. It can also include "mewing," the disputed practice of holding the tongue against the roof of the mouth in hopes of creating a sharper jawline.

Beyond basic grooming, however, the methods can become far more invasive. "Hardmaxxing" may involve cosmetic surgery, anabolic steroids, unapproved peptides, and extreme diets. The most notorious example is "bonesmashing," in which people repeatedly strike their faces, hoping their bones will heal into a more chiseled shape. Medical professionals have warned that this practice can instead cause [fractures, nerve damage, and permanent disfigurement](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38278441/).

Researchers have also raised concerns about how easily looksmaxxing can blur the line between ordinary grooming tips and the ideology of the forums where it originated. A [2025 peer-reviewed study](https://researchportal.port.ac.uk/en/publications/digital-subcultural-diffusion-theory-rebranding-the-incel-ideolog/) argued that the language of science and self-improvement helps ideas from incel communities reach younger users who may initially encounter them as innocent fitness or beauty content.

The movement from niche forums into mainstream youth culture is getting clearer. Consider 20-year-old [looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular](https://mashable.com/article/clavicular-looksmax-incel-explained), whose real name is Braden Peters. He built his following by discussing extreme methods, including steroids, cosmetic procedures, bonesmashing, and, by his own account, using methamphetamine to suppress his appetite.

Now, Clavicular is on a [10-stop college tour](https://onwardstate.com/2026/08/12/content-creator-clavicular-is-coming-to-state-college-this-month/) with events near Penn State, Syracuse, Binghamton, Virginia Tech, Clemson, Coastal Carolina, and Texas A&M — all schools packed with fans in his target demographic. It has been a hit. 700 people were listed as planning to attend his [Syracuse stop](https://linkstub.com/en/cuse-welcome-week-day-2). Before his Binghamton appearance, one participating bar [told students](https://www.bupipedream.com/news/clavicular-appearance-downtown-draws-mixed-response-from-students/182421/) to "Start bone smashing and get that jawline in check because this is going to be a college core memory!"

All of this isn't to say young men are abandoning soap en masse. But its emergence shows how easily the looksmaxxing framework can turn an ordinary choice — even something as basic as whether to use deodorant — into another supposed (and smelly) path toward self-improvement.

entries.title: Trump blasts data center critics: Backwards and poor
entries.content:
![A construction worker places a large lock on a fence outside a data center facility.](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01VU4epeK2ZxlNF1xpAkMs7/hero-image.jpg)

Many Americans don't like data centers.

At the very least, a [majority of U.S. citizens](https://yougov.com/en-us/articles/55438-many-americans-think-data-centers-are-bad-for-the-us-more-oppose-them-locally) don't want one of the dozens of proliferating AI infrastructure projects to end up in their backyard, as complaints of environmental destruction, noise pollution, and water constraints reach a fever pitch.

But President Donald Trump doesn't really care. In a recent Truth Social [post](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117190477440173795), the country's leader called data centers a "golden goose" that Americans would be remiss to push back on.

"The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," the President wrote. "If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign."

SEE ALSO:
[Trump administration acted illegally in fight against Anthropic, judge rules](https://mashable.com/tech/trump-anthropic-ban-illegal-judge-rules)

## Trump doubles down on data centers

The inflammatory post echoed [similar sentiments](https://www.texastribune.org/2026/08/07/donald-trump-texas-data-centers-greg-abbott/) shared earlier this month, as well as arguments he made in [posts from July](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/116924979201330474). In fact, Trump has steadfastly backed large-scale data center projects, despite his own party [backing away](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/27/republicans-breaking-with-trump-data-centers-01051897) from data center commitments on the campaign trail.

"If I were the mayor of a town or the governor of a state, and I had a chance to get a big plant in an AI plant or a data center, I would absolutely want it because the jobs are enormous, and the money paid, the taxes paid are just enormous," said Trump at a recent [convening of cryptocurrency leaders](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-keeps-embracing-data-centers-an-unpopular-topic-in-midterm-races) at the White House.

An anonymous insider told the *Washington Post* that Trump's hardline on leaving AI and data centers unfettered by federal regulation is a "personal" subject for him. "You just can’t change his mind about it," the source told the publication.

Behind the scenes, the Trump administration has been edging open the floodgates to Big Tech-backed data centers as part of his mission to establish a nationwide AI infrastructure to rival China.

In fact, Trump has cited the foreign power regularly in arguments for data center investment. "China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!" said Trump in the Aug. 31 post.

A recent post by the Global Government Affairs team at Elon Musked-owned X alleged that the platform had [uncovered a bot farm network](https://www.engadget.com/2246140/x-chinese-bot-farm-anti-ai-data-center-sentiments/) made up of 200,000 accounts posting anti-data center sentiment. The claims appeared to be based on a recent OpenAI investigation that found several bot accounts using OpenAI's tools to produce such content, but the report also indicated these accounts were sharing genuine news reports about energy concerns.

## How the federal government is enabling data centers

Trump's Big Tech allies have benefited from his [pro-America approach](https://thehill.com/policy/technology/5767824-trump-signs-agreement-with-big-tech-to-cover-data-center-electricity-costs/) to tech advancement. Last year, Trump signed an executive order [fast-tracking federal permitting](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/07/accelerating-federal-permitting-of-data-center-infrastructure/) for AI data centers. The administration has also lobbied for expedited electricity grid connections and pushed for government approvals of new chemicals used for data center manufacturing and facilities.

In an attempt to quell the ensuing community-driven uproar against these projects, the federal government announced a [Ratepayer Protection Pledge](https://mashable.com/article/trump-ai-tech-corps-data-centers-military) with several of AI's biggest players already signed on, committing to offset energy grid costs for local communities.

Still, Big Tech's centers have faced mounting legal pressure, including several lawsuits that claim companies like SpacexAI (formerly xAI) and Microsoft violated pollution-permitting laws in the construction of their facilities. Just last week, non-profit newsroom Floodlight accused a Microsoft-backed data center in New Jersey of [violating federal law](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/aug/27/new-jersey-vineland-datacenter-permits?ref=floodlightnews.org) by operating unpermitted gas-powered generators. The center, known as DataOne, is the first in the state to build its own power plant, the *Guardian* reported. Many centers are shifting to self-sustained power as states [crack down on energy grid connections](https://mashable.com/tech/greg-abbott-texas-data-center-audit).

SEE ALSO:
[The NAACP is fighting back against AI data centers](https://mashable.com/article/naacp-data-centers)

In turn, the federal government has interceded in efforts to enforce environmental law, including levying threats that such attempts pose a "[national security threat](https://mashable.com/tech/justice-department-ai-data-centers-pollution-lawsuit)" for potentially impacting the Department of War's AI capabilities.

Meanwhile, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has been planning to [scrap a federal rule](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/986176/data-center-pollution-epa-rule-change-air-permit) requiring public notice and time for comment when applying for such air permits. The move would effectively shift responsibility for public notice to local agencies and could legitimize the legal violations that communities are invoking to fight back, experts say.

entries.title: Microsoft Outlook outage reported by thousands of users on Monday
entries.content:
![illustration of utility workers next to a laptop with the microsoft outlook logo](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03Nqnn5qPnDFZMOvlZoCbj9/hero-image.png)

Microsoft Outlook appears to be down for a significant number of users as of Monday late morning. According to Downdetector, reports of Outlook problems spiked sharply just before 11:16 a.m. ET, jumping from around 37 reports to over 6,000 in a short window.

![downdetector graph showing user error reports for downdetector](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03Nqnn5qPnDFZMOvlZoCbj9/images-1.fill.size_2000x895.v1788200663.png)

Credit: DownDetector

* ***Last call: Guess what Apple will release in September in our Big Guessing Game: Apple edition. [Enter now for a chance to win an Apple Watch](https://mashable.com/tech/big-guessing-game-apple-edition-round-3)******!***

Of the issues users are reporting, the largest share involves receiving messages, followed by app-related problems and login issues, per Downdetector's tracking. Microsoft acknowledged the outage on its Microsoft 365 Status account on X.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/MSFT365Status/status/2094455556454920701 "(Opens in a new tab)")

The company stated it was investigating reports of Exchange Online issues, pointing users to incident EX1464935 in the admin center for updates.

About an hour later, Microsoft followed up to confirm the scope of the problem, saying it had verified that users may be experiencing degraded functionality across various Exchange Online features. The company said it was reviewing service telemetry and diagnostic data to pin down the root cause.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/MSFT365Status/status/2094465993007378744 "(Opens in a new tab)")

At the time of this writing, Microsoft's status account [posted a more specific update](https://x.com/MSFT365Status/status/2094480650170446254?s=20), stating it had identified an issue with an authentication component that contributed to the disruption. According to the post, Microsoft has “developed a remediation strategy” and is testing it to confirm it resolves the impact before rolling it out more broadly. However, as of this writing, [Microsoft's Service Health Status page](https://status.cloud.microsoft/m365/referrer=serviceStatusRedirect) says that all its products are "currently operational."

Mashable contacted Microsoft with questions about the potential outage, and we'll update this story if we receive a response.

The outage has stirred up plenty of frustration online. On X, users have pushed back on Microsoft's "degraded functionality" language, with [one commenter](https://x.com/BillsandBeers/status/2094502558270128559?s=20) calling it "one way to say 'none of our shit works.'"

Others reported the disruption stretching on for hours, with entire offices and thousands of employees affected worldwide, according to posts under Microsoft's status updates.

A parallel [Reddit thread in r/Outlook](https://www.reddit.com/r/Outlook/comments/1w3ifwe/outlook_down_for_you_all/) saw a similar flood of confirmations from users locked out of the service, with dozens simply chiming in with variations of "down for me" and "yep, whole company having issues."

*This is a developing story...*

entries.title: ValleyRAT: When Legitimate Software Becomes a Malware Delivery Tool
entries.content:
## ValleyRAT hides behind legitimate adware, using DLL sideloading to evade detection, steal data and give Silver Fox control of infected systems.

ValleyRAT doesn’t always need to disguise itself as a cracked game or a fake browser update. It can also hide behind something much more ordinary: an application that looks like adware and appears to serve a legitimate purpose.

Kaspersky’s latest analysis shows how this works. Researchers found a malicious installer that uses a modified version of QN Wallpaper, a legitimate Chinese desktop wallpaper application, to deliver the ValleyRAT backdoor while making the infection look like a normal software installation.

Researchers found a malicious installer that uses a modified version of QN Wallpaper, a legitimate Chinese desktop wallpaper application, to deliver the ValleyRAT backdoor while making the infection look like a normal software installation.

The interesting part is how the attackers make the first stages look harmless. The installer can present itself as software associated with DingTalk, Google Chrome or Tencent Meeting, depending on the filename, while quietly deploying the modified wallpaper application in the background.

That gives the victim something familiar to look at while the real work happens elsewhere. It’s a simple trick, but it removes one of the most obvious warning signs of a malware infection: the feeling that something unusual has just been installed.

Kaspersky originally received one of the samples because a customer wanted it classified as adware. An initial look at the file suggested exactly that, but suspicious network activity changed the picture and led researchers to examine the sample more closely. They found that the advertising component didn’t actually perform its supposed job. Instead, it started an infection chain that eventually loaded ValleyRAT.

*“The original version of QN Wallpaper is genuine adware: on installation, it delivers bundled partner apps to the device and then displays ad banners to the user.” [reads Kaspersky’s report.](https://securelist.com/valleyrat-backdoor-adware/121175/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) “In this case, however, the attackers use it to carry out DLL sideloading, a technique that allows malicious code to run under the guise of a signed process by way of a malicious DLL.”*

That distinction matters because the attackers aren’t inventing a fake application from scratch. They’re abusing software that already looks legitimate and using its normal execution flow to load malicious code.

The technique is [DLL sideloading](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/dll-sideloading-2). In simple terms, the attacker places a malicious DLL where a legitimate program expects to find a library, allowing the trusted application to load the attacker’s code.

Here, the relevant library is `libcef.dll`. QN Wallpaper and its companion process load that library when they start, giving the attackers a convenient place to execute their own code under the name of a legitimate application.

The installer also creates persistence and disables Windows Defender through the `DisableAntiSpyware` registry key before launching QnWallpaper.exe. That combination makes the infection considerably more serious than ordinary adware.

Once the malicious library runs, it checks whether the current user has administrator privileges. If necessary, it attempts to relaunch the process with elevated privileges before continuing with the next stage.

The actual ValleyRAT payload sits encrypted inside the infection chain. Depending on which legitimate process loads the malicious library, the backdoor comes from either a separate `PeLoader` file or resources embedded in `libcef.dll`.

The payloads use AES encryption and contain ValleyRAT as an encrypted DLL. Their configurations differ mainly in the command-and-control addresses they use, giving the operators more than one way to manage infected systems.

ValleyRAT then starts behaving like the backdoor it actually is. It reads its configuration, connects to its command-and-control infrastructure and prepares a range of functions that give an attacker control over the compromised machine.

The malware can collect keystrokes and clipboard contents, monitor the active window and gather detailed information about the infected system. That includes the hostname, IP addresses, Windows version, CPU information, available disk space, graphics adapter, language settings and other system details.

*“The backdoor also has spyware functionality. While running, it tracks keystrokes and the currently focused window by using functions from the DirectInput8 library. It also captures clipboard contents.” continues the report. “All collected data is saved to a file on disk.”*

The operator can also order the backdoor to take screenshots, reboot or shut down the machine, wipe logs, change its command-and-control addresses and download additional modules. ValleyRAT can retrieve those modules from either its own C2 infrastructure or a third-party address.

That last capability gives the attackers room to change what the malware does after the initial infection. They don’t need to put every capability into the first payload if they can download new components later.

The malware also takes steps to make itself harder to remove. Depending on its configuration, it can inject code into `svchost.exe` so that the backdoor restarts if someone stops it. It can also mark its own process as critical, meaning that terminating it can trigger a system crash.

That’s not subtle, but it’s effective. The malware is essentially telling the defender that killing the process isn’t supposed to be a clean operation.

Kaspersky says ValleyRAT can detect security and traffic-analysis tools, while the campaign has been detected over 100,000 times in 2026, affecting more than 1,500 users, mainly in China and India. The activity is linked to Silver Fox, focused on both espionage and financial gain.

In July 2026, Cato CTRL [documented](https://securityaffairs.com/196347/apt/silverfox-targets-japanese-manufacturer-with-advanced-valleyrat-campaign.html) a [SilverFox](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/silverfox) campaign targeting a Japanese industrial manufacturer. The attack chain adds two previously undocumented DLL-sideloading hosts, two kernel drivers not previously associated with SilverFox, and a dual-layer recovery architecture that keeps ValleyRAT running even if defenders terminate individual components.

That broader activity puts the Kaspersky finding into perspective. The adware campaign isn’t an isolated curiosity. It fits a larger pattern in which Silver Fox uses legitimate software, familiar brands and trusted execution paths to get malicious code onto Windows systems and keep it there.

For defenders, blocking a known ValleyRAT file is not enough because the real risk is how the malware gets executed. A legitimate-looking application, signed component or familiar installer can become part of a malicious chain. Antivirus exclusions can make the problem worse by creating blind spots.

*“This case is a clear example of how adware and affiliate networks can turn out to be far more dangerous than they appear. ValleyRAT is a sophisticated backdoor capable of collecting sensitive data such as keystrokes and clipboard contents, taking screenshots, and delivering additional malicious modules.” concludes the report. “The attackers exploited a well-known adware application to run the backdoor under the guise of a signed process, which complicates detection.”*

Kaspersky recommends clear rules for third-party software, security awareness and avoiding suspicious applications or exclusions simply because a program asks for them. The malware does not need to look dangerous; it only needs to look legitimate enough that nobody questions why an ordinary application suddenly behaves like a backdoor.

entries.title: Broadcom Pledges to Lock Down Open Source Python, Java Libraries
entries.content:
Broadcom is launching "TrueSource," an effort to curate and secure open-source components used with its Tanzu platform, including Spring, RabbitMQ, and libraries across Java, Python, and Node.js. "The idea is to provide a set of solutions focused on providing clean and secure artefacts," Purnima Padmanabhan, vice president of Broadcom's Tanzu Division, told The Register. "We choose and build every Spring library, databases, other Java components," she said. The Register reports: Padmanabhan said that promise means VMware will also provide "TrueSource trusted artifacts" for code that is not part of Spring, including the wider Java ecosystem, Python, and Node.js. "Broadcom's curation process ensures that the libraries conform to a reference architecture and are supportable by the maintainers of record," according to a company statement. "Thousands of engineers across Broadcom's software divisions scan, fix, contribute to, and consume them every day."
A VMware spokesperson told The Register the Broadcom business unit "will work with and support maintainers on open source software and we will provide fixes to open source upstream for any active projects." "With Spring and RabbitMQ, we are the maintainers. For other open source software, we will work with the maintainers. We believe that the community maintainers must remain the source of truth," the spokesperson said.
This is just the sort of contribution that the open-source community wants vendors to do to reflect the value they extract from software they did not create alone. It's also the sort of thing vendors sometimes conclude they need to do to keep products based on FOSS viable.
